Applied to persons: "sound/upright ones" (12:101, 21:75, 4:69). Crucially the same participle is used non-morally: "in aataytanaa saalihan" (7:189-190) = "if You give us a SOUND [well-formed] child"; "kaana abuuhumaa saalihan" (18:82); "takuunuu qawman saalihiin" (12:9) = "you will become a people in good/sound standing" after removing Joseph. These physical/relational uses show the residue is soundness-of-condition, not merely piety.

FORM IV aslaha / islaah / muslih (causative) — "put/bring into sound condition." With a plain object: "yuslih lakum aamaalakum" (33:71, set your deeds right), "aslaha baalahum" (47:2, 47:5, set their state right), "aslahnaa lahu zawjahu" (21:90, made his wife sound/fit to bear), "laa yuslihu aamala l-mufsidiin" (10:81, God will not make sound the corrupters' work), "aslih lii fii dhurriyyatii" (46:15). Absolutely (after repentance): "taabuu wa-aslahuu" (2:160, 3:89, 4:146, 5:39, 24:5, 16:119, 6:48, 6:54, 7:35) = "repented and set [themselves] right." With the construction bayna: "aslaha baynahum" / "aslihuu bayna" (2:182, 2:224, 4:35, 4:128, 49:9, 49:10, 8:1, 4:114) = bring the between-relation into sound order = reconcile. The verbal noun islaah (2:220 orphans, 2:228, 4:35, 7:56/7:85 "after its islaah/setting-in-order") and the agent muslih/muslihuun (2:11, 11:117, 28:19, 7:170, 2:220) name the setting-right and the setter-right.

THE INTERNAL ANCHOR: SlH stands in explicit, repeated opposition to FSD (fasad/mufsiduun). "laa tufsiduu fii l-ardi baada islaahihaa" (7:56, 7:85: do not SPOIL the land after its being SET-RIGHT); "innamaa nahnu muslihuun" answering "laa tufsiduu" (2:11); "yufsiduuna fii l-ardi wa-laa yuslihuun" (26:152, 27:48); "al-mufsida mina l-muslih" (2:220); "amiltum al-saalihaat ... ka-l-mufsidiin" (38:28). This antonym pair fixes the direction: SlH = un-spoiled sound right-order; FSD = spoilage/corruption. Because fasad covers both moral and physical/functional spoiling, salaah correspondingly covers moral righteousness AND physical/relational soundness under one center.
SlH.strongest_counterexample: The proper name Salih (Prophet of Thamud): 11:61, 11:62, 11:66, 11:89, 26:142, 27:45, 7:73, 7:75, 7:77 (9 PN occurrences). Here the root makes no compositional contribution to the sentence — the word simply designates a person ("yaa Saalih 'tinaa..." 7:77). This is the hardest case because a rigid designator is semantically bleached: one cannot subtract form/construction/context and be left with an operative "soundness" meaning in the utterance. It RECONCILES rather than contradicts because the name is morphologically identical to the active participle saalih and transparently lexicalizes exactly the root residue ("the sound/upright one"); the soundness sense is thus present at the naming layer and is nowhere negated. It is not placed in inconsistent_refs because the residue is recoverable (indeed etymologically transparent) and never contradicted — only referentially dormant. This is the single point that keeps the disposition from being maximally clean.

SrT.candidate_root_contribution: A single delineated traversable roadway — a bounded course/thoroughfare along which one proceeds from a starting point toward a destination. The root names the physical medium-of-passage itself (the road), not the direction of travel, the quality of the road, or the goal reached; those are supplied by construction (إلى/على/عن), by attributive modifiers (مستقيم, سوي, الجحيم), and by context.
SrT.plain_explanation: Every one of the 45 occurrences is the noun صِرَاط, and in each the recoverable invariant is "a road/route to be walked." The most decisive evidence is the small set of occurrences where the surrounding theology strips away and a bare, near-physical road remains: 7:86 warns highwaymen not to "sit by every road" (بِكُلِّ صِرَاطٍ) to intercept believers — this is a literal thoroughfare where travelers pass; 7:16 has Iblīs vow to "sit on your road" (صِرَاطَكَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ) to ambush; 36:66 pictures people who, blinded, would "race along the road" (فَٱسْتَبَقُوا۟ ٱلصِّرَاطَ) yet cannot see it — a road as a physically negotiated surface. These anchor the concrete core: a course one physically traverses. From this base the abstract 'way of life / religion' sense is an internally bridged extension: 6:153 explicitly places صِرَاطِى (my road, singular) in contrast with ٱلسُّبُل (the branching ways one must not follow), i.e. the same road-image used for a course of conduct. That the root supplies only the road — never the direction — is shown by 37:23, where the identical noun points toward Hell (إِلَىٰ صِرَاطِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ): the road can lead anywhere, so the destination is contributed by إلى + genitive, not by ص ر ط. Likewise the pervasive مُّسْتَقِيم ('straight') is a separate attribute (root qwm): the noun occurs bare and un-straight in 23:74 (عَنِ ٱلصِّرَاطِ لَنَاكِبُونَ — deviating off the road), 36:66, 38:22 (سَوَآءِ ٱلصِّرَاطِ — the even middle of the road), and 7:86, proving straightness is added, not intrinsic. The prepositions map cleanly onto a road-schema: إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ (guidance TO / onto a road: 1:6, 2:142, 6:87, 5:16, 16:121, 24:46, 42:52, 22:24, 37:23, etc.), عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ (being ON/standing upon the road: 11:56 of the Lord, 36:4, 43:43, 67:22, 6:39, 16:76), and عَنِ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ (turning OFF the road: 23:74). Even the hardest cases resolve to 'road': 15:41 (صِرَٰطٌ عَلَىَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ) = a road that runs straight up to / is incumbent upon Me; 11:56 (رَبِّى عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ) = the Lord stands upon a straight road (i.e. His governance runs a straight course). In every family — literal ambush-road, guidance-destination road, standing-upon road, road-to-Hell, the even-middle-of-the-road — subtracting form (invariant: all N), construction (the preposition/case vector), participants, and context leaves exactly one thing: the traversable roadway.
SrT.strongest_counterexample: The hardest occurrence is 15:41: قَالَ هَٰذَا صِرَٰطٌ عَلَىَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ. On one reading صِرَاط here shades toward 'a binding rule/principle upon Me,' which could look like an abstract obligation rather than a road. But it reconciles cleanly without abandoning the residue: the construction عَلَىَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ describes a road that runs straight up to / terminates at the speaker (God) — 'a road [leading] straight to Me' — parallel to the physical على-road frames in 11:56 (رَبِّى عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ) and 36:4. The apparent 'obligation/incumbency' nuance is contributed by the preposition عَلَىٰ + 1st-person pronoun, not by the noun; strip it and the road-image remains. So the residue is recoverable, and the seeming abstraction is a construction effect. (Runner-up hard case, 37:23 صِرَٰطِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ, is actually confirmatory: a road to Hell shows the root supplies only the road, never a positive destination.)

Swm.candidate_root_contribution: A bounded, self-committed ABSTAINING — the deliberate holding-back of oneself from an activity one would otherwise engage in, sustained over a dedicated/consecrated span. The root contributes only the abstention/withholding-of-self vector; WHICH activity is withheld (eating/drinking/marital relations vs. speech) is supplied by context, not by the root.
Swm.plain_explanation: Across the data the constant left after subtracting form and context is "deliberately withholding oneself from a normally-available activity for a set, dedicated period." The single most decisive occurrence is 19:26, where Mary declares "إِنِّى نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ صَوْمًا فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ ... إِنسِيًّا" — here صَوْم is explicitly a vow of SILENCE (abstention from speaking), involving no food at all. This proves the root itself does not mean "not eating"; it means "abstaining/holding back," with the object of abstention being contextually filled (here, speech). The ritual occurrences then instantiate the same residue with a different object: 2:183 ٱلصِّيَامُ prescribed on believers; the two verbs 2:184 تَصُومُوا۟ and 2:185 فَلْيَصُمْهُ (perform the abstention / abstain through the month); 2:187 defines the temporal bounds of the abstention ("لَيْلَةَ ٱلصِّيَامِ ... أَتِمُّوا۟ ٱلصِّيَامَ إِلَى ٱلَّيْلِ" — a daylight-bounded holding-back from food, drink, and رَفَث). The expiation cluster (2:196 صِيَامٍ / فَصِيَامُ, 4:92 فَصِيَامُ شَهْرَيْنِ, 58:4 فَصِيَامُ شَهْرَيْنِ, 5:89 فَصِيَامُ ثَلَٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍ, 5:95 صِيَامًا) all present a bounded stretch of self-withholding offered as a substitute act. The active participle in 33:35 (ٱلصَّٰٓئِمِينَ وَٱلصَّٰٓئِمَٰتِ) names people characterized by this habitual self-abstaining. Every form-family (verbal noun صوم/صيام, finite verb يصوم/تصوموا, participle صائم) and every sense-family (narrative vow of silence, prescribed Ramadan fast, juridical expiation, eschatological virtue) reduces to the same core: bounded, dedicated withholding-of-self.
Swm.strongest_counterexample: 19:26 (صَوْمًا = a vow of silence) is simultaneously the hardest case and the interpretive key. It is hardest because it superficially breaks the ritual-fast reading: no food, drink, or marital abstention is in view — the withheld activity is speech. But it reconciles perfectly with, and in fact establishes, the abstract residue: the root supplies "abstaining/holding-back," and the object of that abstaining is context-filled. Rather than being an anomaly, it is the internal evidence that forces the abstraction and rules out a food-specific core. It is fully reconciled by layer-subtraction (the object "speech" belongs to the context layer).

bdl.candidate_root_contribution: SUBSTITUTION: the relation in which one entity comes to stand in the place of another — a counterpart displacing an original, such that where item A was, item B now is. The root supplies only the substitution relation itself (one-for-another, put-in-place-of); it does NOT by itself fix the direction (which item is original vs. replacement), the evaluative polarity (upgrade vs. downgrade), or the domain — those come from construction, participants, and context.
bdl.plain_explanation:
Across every form-family the invariant is "B comes to stand where A was." This is repeatedly made explicit by three overlapping construction markers, but the substitution relation is present even when unmarked:

(1) makāna ("in the place of") — 16:101 "baddalnā āyatan makāna āyatin" (We substitute one sign IN PLACE OF another); 7:95 "baddalnā makāna al-sayyiʾati al-ḥasanata" (We put good IN PLACE OF evil); 4:20 "istibdāla zawjin makāna zawjin" (replacement of one wife IN PLACE OF another). These pin the core meaning precisely: an item installed where another stood.

(2) ghayr ("other than") — 2:59 / 7:162 "baddala ... qawlan ghayra alladhī qīla lahum" (substituted a word OTHER THAN what was said); 4:56 "baddalnāhum julūdan ghayrahā" (replaced them with OTHER skins); 14:48 "tubaddalu al-arḍu ghayra al-arḍ" (the earth is exchanged for OTHER than the earth); 47:38 / 9:39 "yastabdil qawman ghayrakum" (replace you with an OTHER people). The replacer is explicitly the not-original.

(3) bi- / accusative of exchange (A-for-B) — 4:2 "tatabaddalū al-khabītha bil-ṭayyib" (take the bad IN EXCHANGE FOR the good); 2:108 "yatabaddal al-kufra bil-īmān" (takes disbelief for faith); 2:61 "atastabdilūna alladhī huwa adnā bi-alladhī huwa khayr" (exchange the lower FOR the better); 33:52 "an tabaddala bihinna min azwāj" (exchange them for other wives).

Form-family coverage of the same relation:
- V(II) baddala (transitive/causative substitution): "yubaddilu ... sayyiʾātihim ḥasanāt" (25:70, replaces their evil deeds with good), "yubaddilannahum ... khawfihim amnan" (24:55, replaces their fear with security), 34:16 gardens replaced by inferior gardens, 40:26 "yubaddila dīnakum" (change/replace your religion), 48:15 "yubaddilū kalāma Allāh" (alter = substitute-for God's speech), 50:29 "mā yubaddalu al-qawlu ladayya" (the sentence is not swapped out before Me), 56:61/70:41/76:28 "nubaddila ... amthālakum / khayran minhum" (replace you with your likes / better).
- V(IV) abdala (provide-in-exchange): 18:81, 66:5, 68:32 "yubdila(humā/hu/nā) khayran minhu/minhā/minkunna" — God gives a better one IN PLACE OF what was lost.
- V(V) tabaddala (take-for-self in exchange): 2:108, 4:2, 33:52 — subject acquires B while giving up A.
- V(X)/N(X) istabdala / istibdāl (seek/effect substitution): 2:61, 47:38, 9:39, 4:20.
- N(II) tabdīl / mubaddil (act / agent of substitution): the negated "lā tabdīla / lā mubaddila li-kalimāti(hi) / li-khalqi llāh / li-sunnati llāh" (10:64, 18:27, 6:115, 6:34, 30:30, 33:62, 35:43, 48:23) = God's words/creation/way admit NO substitution — nothing can be installed in their place; "mā baddalū tabdīlan" (33:23) = they effected no swap of their commitment.
- ADJ/noun badal (the substitute item): 18:50 "biʾsa lil-ẓālimīna badalan" — Iblis and his offspring are a wretched SUBSTITUTE (taken as protectors in place of God).

In every case, subtracting form and construction leaves the same residue: one thing standing in the place of another.
bdl.strongest_counterexample: The hardest cases are those where no second (replacer) item is surfaced and the sense looks like bare "change/alteration" rather than "A-for-B substitution": 33:23 "wa-mā baddalū tabdīlan" (they did not change [their commitment] in the least) and the immutability formulas 30:30 "lā tabdīla li-khalqi llāh," 50:29 "mā yubaddalu al-qawlu ladayya," 33:62/35:43/48:23 "lā tajidu li-sunnati llāhi tabdīlan." Here only ONE item (the covenant, creation, the decree, the sunna) is named. Reconciliation: these are all NEGATED or steadfastness contexts, and negated substitution still presupposes the substitution relation — "no tabdīl" means precisely "nothing installed in its place," "no counterpart admitted," which is why 35:43 can immediately contrast it with taḥwīl (diverting-away): the two negations deny two distinct operations. The counterpart (the would-be replacer) is implicit but structurally required — you cannot "swap out X" without an incoming Y, even if Y is left unspecified. So these reduce to "the relation whereby a counterpart takes X's place — here asserted impossible," not to a rootless notion of qualitative modification. The residue holds.

bny.candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes the notion of a CONSTITUTED, RAISED-UP ENTITY that issues from and stands upon a foundational source — a "built-up product" together with its constitutive dependence on that source. Concretely: (a) with the building family, a structure erected upon a base (bunyān/binā'/ṣarḥ/bayt/samā' raised min al-qawā'id or 'alā a footing); (b) with the kinship family, a child/descendant as the generatively "built-up" issue and standing extension of a progenitor (ibn/banū/banāt/abnā'). The invariant residue is: derived-standing-entity + its source-relation (source → constituted continuation).
bny.plain_explanation: Two surface sense-families appear, and the invariant sits underneath both. (1) BUILDING. The 11 verbal occurrences all denote erecting a standing structure: "ibnū 'alayhim bunyānā" (18:21) build a structure over them; "ibni lī ṣarḥan" (40:36) build me a tower; "ibni lī 'indaka baytan" (66:11) build me a house; "wa-l-samā'a banaynāhā bi-aydin" (51:47), "banaynā fawqakum sab'an shidādan" (78:12), "am al-samā'u banāhā" (79:27) — the raised sky; "bunyānuhum alladhī banaw" (9:110) the structure they built. The building nouns match: bunyān raised "min al-qawā'id" from the foundations (16:26), "asasa bunyānahu 'alā taqwā" founded his structure upon (9:109), "al-samā' binā'an" the sky as a raised canopy (2:22; 40:64), bannā' the builder (38:37), ghuraf mabniyya built chambers (39:20), bunyān marṣūṣ a compacted structure (61:4). In every case: an entity raised so as to stand, resting on / issuing from a base. (2) KINSHIP. The 173 nominal occurrences overwhelmingly denote offspring/descendants: ibn Maryam, banū Isrā'īl, banū Ādam, abnā'akum, banāt, banūn/banīn ("al-mālu wa-l-banūn" 18:46). Subtracting form and construction, the residue is the same shape: the child is the constituted issue that stands as the continuation of its progenitor-source. This is confirmed INTERNALLY by two pivot usages: "ibn al-sabīl" (2:177; 9:60; 17:26; 8:41…) — the traveler, literally "offspring of the road," where no biological birth is involved and the term can only mean "one constitutively derived-from / belonging-to X"; and the group term "banū Isrā'īl / banū Ādam," a whole lineage raised up from a single named source. These show that "ibn/banū" encodes "constituted-issue-of-a-source," exactly the abstraction the building family instantiates physically. Even the polemical cases fit: "naḥnu abnā'u llāh" (5:18), "'Uzayr ibn Allāh / al-Masīḥ ibn Allāh" (9:30) assert precisely a source-constitution relation, and "mā ja'ala ad'iyā'akum abnā'akum" (33:4) denies that adoption creates the genuine built-from-you relation — the residue is the very thing being affirmed or denied.
bny.strongest_counterexample: The single hardest case is the pure construction cluster, e.g. "wa-l-samā'a banaynāhā bi-aydin" (51:47:2:1) and "ibni lī ṣarḥan" (40:36:4:1), set against the ~160 pure-kinship occurrences: the two evoke visibly different images (masonry vs. begetting), which threatens to split the root into two homonyms rather than one residue. It reconciles because the internal data itself supplies the bridge: "ibn al-sabīl" (e.g. 2:177:27:2) proves "ibn" is NOT restricted to biological birth but means "constitutively derived-from / belonging-to X," and "banū Isrā'īl / banū Ādam" name whole lineages raised from one source — so the kinship family already trades in the abstract "constituted-issue-from-a-base" that the building family renders physically. The shared residue (derived standing-entity + source-relation) is genuinely recoverable in the construction cases (a structure raised upon its qawā'id) and the kinship cases (a descendant raised from a progenitor) alike; nothing contradicts it. The reconciliation is real but requires an abstraction step, which is why the strength is capped at MODERATE.

dbr.candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes the notion of THE HIND/REAR — the back-side, or that which lies behind / comes after (spatially, sequentially, or temporally): the rear as a locus (a body's back, a garment's back, the hindmost tail-end of a group), the direction "toward the rear/backward," and by extension the "back-end / after / outcome" of an event or matter. Every occurrence names, faces toward, moves toward, arrives at, or attends to this rear/after pole.
dbr.plain_explanation: Six form/sense families all resolve to a single "rear / behind / after" residue. (A) Anatomical/physical rear (form N, dubur/adbaar): the shirt torn "min dubur" = from the back (12:25:6:1, 12:27:6:1, 12:28:6:1); striking "their faces and their backs" (8:50:10:2, 47:27:7:2); "he turns his back / they turn the backs" in flight (8:16:4:1 dubura-hu, 54:45:4:2 al-dubur, 3:111:8:2, 8:15:11:2, 33:15:9:2, 48:22:6:2, 59:12:13:2 al-adbaar); "reverting upon their backs" = going backward (17:46:18:1, 47:25:5:1, 5:21:12:1, 4:47:18:1); "follow behind their rears" (15:65:7:1). Here the residue is fully surface-visible: dubur = the back. (B) Hindmost extremity / tail-end (form N, daabir): "the daabir of the wrongdoing people was cut off" = the very last/rearmost trace extirpated (6:45:2:1, 7:72:7:1, 8:7:22:1, 15:66:6:1); daabir = "that which comes hindmost." (C) Temporal after/going-behind: "the adbaar (aftermaths/ends) of prostration" (50:40:4:2) and "the idbaar (going-behind/setting) of the stars" (52:49:4:2) — the rear applied to time: the after-part of an act, the receding of the stars behind the horizon. (D) Form IV adbara / participle mudbir = to present the back, hence recede/turn away: "then he turned his back" (74:23:2:1, 79:22:2:1, 70:17:3:1), "the night when it retreats/turns its back" (74:33:3:1), and the mudbir cluster "they turned away, backs-turned" (21:57:7:1, 27:10:9:1, 27:80:11:1, 28:31:10:1, 30:52:11:1, 37:90:3:1, 40:33:3:1, 9:25:23:1). Here the root supplies the "rear/back," and Form IV supplies "give/show the back" → recede. (E) Form II dabbara / participle mudabbiraat = to attend to the back-ends/outcomes of a matter, i.e. dispose/manage it: "He directs the affair" (10:3:15:1, 10:31:21:1, 13:2:19:1, 32:5:1:1) and "those managing the affair" (79:5:1:3). The residue "the after/outcome of the amr" is reached through the internally-attested "rear=after/end" bridge (see families B and C). (F) Form V tadabbara = to make oneself examine the back-ends/consequences of discourse → ponder deeply: "do they not reflect on the Qur'an / the saying / its verses" (4:82:2:1, 47:24:2:1, 23:68:2:1, 38:29:5:2) — the reflexive of family E's "attend to what lies behind/after the words."
dbr.strongest_counterexample: The Form II "manage/direct the affair" cluster — "yudabbiru l-amr" (10:3:15:1, 10:31:21:1, 13:2:19:1, 32:5:1:1) and "al-mudabbiraat amran" (79:5:1:3) — is the single hardest case, because on the surface "govern/direct" shows no visible "back." It reconciles through a bridge that is itself internally attested, not imported from outside: the same data independently establish "rear = tail-end/after/outcome" (daabir = the hindmost trace cut off, 6:45/7:72/8:7/15:66; adbaar al-sujood = the after of prostration, 50:40; idbaar al-nujoom = the stars going behind, 52:49). Reading dabbara as "to attend to and set the back-ends/outcomes of the affair" therefore recovers the residue from within the packet. The reconciliation is genuine but requires conceptual extension, so it does not count as a clean surface presence.

fqr.candidate_root_contribution: A deficit/breach in self-sufficient wholeness — the root marks a subject (or the infliction) of being broken below the level of complete, standing sufficiency, i.e. lacking the resource/integrity needed to stand on one's own. In the participant/state family (faqīr, fuqarāʾ, faqr) this surfaces as "one/state characterized by a shortfall of means → needy, destitute"; in the event family (fāqira) it surfaces as "an event that ruptures wholeness → a shattering, back-breaking blow." The root supplies the DEFICIT/RUPTURE-OF-WHOLENESS pole, never the sufficiency itself.
fqr.plain_explanation: Two form-families exhaust the data. FAMILY A — the faqīr/fuqarāʾ/faqr cluster (13 of 14) — is anchored internally by its repeated, explicit opposition to ghinā/ghaniyy (self-sufficiency/wealth), which makes the residue "shortfall of sufficient means" surface-recoverable: 3:181 quotes the disbelievers "inna llāha faqīrun wa-naḥnu aghniyāʾ" (God is faqīr, we are rich) — faqīr = ascribed a deficit set against aghniyāʾ; 4:135 "in yakun ghaniyyan aw faqīran" and 4:6 "wa-man kāna ghaniyyan… wa-man kāna faqīran" pair the two poles directly; 35:15 "antumu l-fuqarāʾu ilā llāhi wa-llāhu huwa l-ghaniyy" and 47:38 "wa-llāhu l-ghaniyyu wa-antumu l-fuqarāʾ" set human deficit against divine sufficiency. The alms verses designate the faqīr as the licensed recipient precisely because he is in deficit: 9:60 "innamā l-ṣadaqātu lil-fuqarāʾi wa-l-masākīn…", 2:271, 2:273 "lil-fuqarāʾi lladhīna uḥṣirū fī sabīli llāh", 59:8 "lil-fuqarāʾi l-muhājirīn", 22:28 "wa-aṭʿimū l-bāʾisa l-faqīr". 24:32 "in yakūnū fuqarāʾa yughnihimu llāhu min faḍlih" is decisive: the state fqr is the very thing removed by God making them ghaniyy (yughni-him). 2:268 "al-shayṭānu yaʿidukumu l-faqra" abstracts the same as the state-noun (poverty). 28:24 "innī limā anzalta ilayya min khayrin faqīr" = "I am in deficit of / in need of whatever good You send me" — with the construction ilā/li supplying the directed-dependency vector, the root itself still contributes only the deficit. FAMILY B — fāqira (75:25) "taẓunnu an yufʿala bihā fāqiratun" — an event done TO the gloomy faces: a back-breaking calamity. Subtracting the fāʿila event-noun morphology, the residue is the same deficit/breach, now realized as an act that ruptures a subject's wholeness rather than a standing state of lack. Across both families the invariant left after removing morphology, construction, participants and context is: a breach/deficit of self-sufficient wholeness.
fqr.strongest_counterexample: 75:25:5:1 (fāqira). It is the single occurrence outside the poverty/need cluster: "taẓunnu an yufʿala bihā fāqiratun" describes a back-breaking calamity inflicted on the gloomy faces, not a state of material lack. It reconciles by reading the fāʿila event-noun morphology over the same root deficit: fāqira = an act that RUPTURES a subject's wholeness/integrity (breaks the back), which is the event-side of the very "breach of self-sufficient wholeness" that, on the state-side, yields faqīr = one whose means are broken below sufficiency. The reconciliation is genuine but INFERENTIAL: with only one fāqira token and no internal verse bridging "breaking" to "lack", the shared "rupture-of-wholeness" center is recovered by abstraction from the form, not demonstrated by an attested internal link. Hence unity holds here but at the abstract altitude, not the surface.

krm.candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes ELEVATED INTRINSIC WORTH: the marking of an entity as being of high, esteem-commanding value/nobility/excellence. In stative-adjectival forms it names the quality (a bearer that is precious, noble, honorable, choice); in causative-verbal and derived-nominal forms it names the conferring or recognition of that elevated-worth status upon a participant (to raise into / treat as possessing high worth = to honor/ennoble).
krm.plain_explanation: Every occurrence, once form/construction/participant/context are subtracted, leaves the same residue: "of high, esteem-worthy value." (1) The dominant adjective kareem/kiraam attributes this worth across radically different participants — an angel (12:31 malak kareem), speech (17:23 qawlan kareeman), provision and reward (22:50; 33:31 rizq/ajr kareem), a throne (23:116 al-ʿarsh al-kareem), a station (26:58 maqaam kareem), a choice/noble kind of plant (26:7; 31:10 zawj kareem), a letter (27:29 kitaab kareem), scripture (56:77 qurʾaan kareem), a messenger (44:17; 69:40; 81:19 rasool kareem), and God Himself (44:49 al-kareem; 82:6; 96:3 al-akram). In each the item is not merely present but marked as high-value/noble/excellent. (2) The elative akram (49:13 akramakum ʿind Allah = the most elevated-in-worth before God = the most pious; 96:3 al-akram = the supremely worthy) is the same quality at superlative degree. (3) The plural substantive kiraam works identically: noble recording angels (82:11 kiraaman kaatibin; 80:16 kiraam barara) and people of dignified comportment (25:72 marru kiraaman = passed by with nobility). (4) The causative verbs karrama (17:70 karramnaa banii aadama = ennobled/gave-worth to the sons of Adam; 17:62 Iblis: "this one whom You karramta ʿalayya" = elevated in worth above me) and akrama (12:21 akrimii mathwaahu = give-worth to his lodging = treat him honorably; 89:15 rabbii akramani = my Lord raised me in worth; 89:17 laa tukrimoona al-yateem = you do not accord worth to the orphan) all denote conferring the krm-quality on someone. (5) The passive/derived nouns mukramoon / mukrameen / mukarrama / ikraam are the received or bestowed form of that same status: honored servants (21:26; 37:42; 70:35), the honored (36:27), Abraham's honored guests (51:24), honored scrolls (80:13 mukarrama), and God as dhu'l-jalaali wa'l-ikraam (55:27; 55:78 = Possessor of Majesty and the according-of-worth). The single invariant is therefore "elevated, esteem-worthy value," with the verb/nominal families adding only the causative/recognitional direction supplied by their morphology.
krm.strongest_counterexample: The hardest case is 56:44:4:1 "laa baaridin wa laa kareem" — the shade/repast of the damned is "neither cool nor kareem." Here krm is (a) negated and (b) predicated of an unpleasant inanimate thing, which could look like a bare sense of "good/beneficial" rather than "worth/nobility." It reconciles cleanly: negation operates ON the invariant, not against it — the verse denies that the item possesses any esteem-worthy/beneficial value, so the residue "elevated worth" is exactly what is being withheld. The polarity is supplied by laa (construction); the residue is untouched. A secondary hard case, 89:15's akramani read against the following ahaanani (debased me), corroborates the residue: krm is the raising-in-worth whose lexical opposite is debasement, confirming direction (up in worth), not mere giving.

lwm.candidate_root_contribution: The imputation of fault/censure onto an agent for a deed — i.e., holding someone answerable-at-fault and expressing that as reproach/blame. The root supplies a directed evaluative act of fault-attribution (blame), independent of who directs it (another, a reciprocal group, or the self) and of whether the residue surfaces as the act, the agent doing it, or the state of being its target.
lwm.plain_explanation:
Every occurrence resolves to the single notion "blame / reproach = imputing fault to an agent for something done."

FORM I active verb (blaming as an act): 12:32:4:1 لُمْتُنَّنِى "you (women) blamed me concerning him" (Potiphar's wife); 14:22:25:1 تَلُومُونِى "do not blame me" and 14:22:26:2 لُومُوا أَنفُسَكُم "blame your own selves" (Satan redirecting culpability). Here the root is transparently the verbal act of fault-attribution, and the same act is even turned reflexive ("blame yourselves").

FORM VI reciprocal verb (mutual blaming): 68:30:5:1 يَتَلَاوَمُونَ — the ruined garden-owners "blaming one another." Pure directed fault-attribution, now bidirectional; the VI morphology supplies the reciprocity, the root supplies the blame.

PASSIVE PARTICIPLE مَلُوم (state of being the target of blame): 17:29:12:1 and 17:39:17:1 مَلُومًا (sitting/cast down "blamed"); 23:6:10:1 & 70:30:10:1 غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ ("not blamed" re lawful spouses); 51:54:5:2 فَمَا أَنتَ بِمَلُومٍ ("you are not to be blamed"). The residue is the imputable-fault-censure whose target is either affirmed or negated.

FORM IV participle مُلِيم (agent who has brought blame upon himself / is culpable): 37:142:4:1 (Jonah, swallowed "while mulīm") and 51:40:7:1 (Pharaoh cast in the sea "while mulīm"). The IV morphology adds "having done that which incurs X"; the X is still blame — one in a state of deserved fault-censure.

ACTIVE PARTICIPLE + INSTANCE NOUN (the blamer and an act of blame): 5:54:27–28 لَوْمَةَ لَآئِمٍ "the blame of any blamer" — لَوْمَة is a single act of censure, لَآئِم the one who censures.

INTENSIVE ADJECTIVE (habitual self-reproach): 75:2:4:2 النَّفْس اللَّوَّامَة "the ever-reproaching soul" — intensive form of the same fault-imputing act, turned on the self.

Across active/reciprocal verbs, passive/active participles, instance and intensive nominals, the constant left after subtracting morphology is: directed attribution of fault = blame.
lwm.strongest_counterexample: The Form IV participle مُلِيم (37:142:4:1 Jonah; 51:40:7:1 Pharaoh) is the hardest, because unlike مَلُوم ("one blamed by someone") it is not obviously a passive target of blame — no blamer is named, and Jonah/Pharaoh are described as mulīm at the very moment of divine seizure, not while being verbally reproached. It reconciles cleanly through layer-subtraction: Form IV of this root is the standard "do/become such as to incur X" pattern (cf. أذنب "commit a sin"), so مُلِيم = "one who has brought blame upon himself / stands culpable." The root residue "fault-imputable censure" is still present — it is the very thing incurred. The morphology (IV) supplies "having earned," the root supplies "blame." So it strengthens rather than breaks the unity: the residue survives even where no external blamer is present, showing the core is fault-attribution itself, not merely the social speech-act.

nsy.candidate_root_contribution: A previously-possessed content (a fact, obligation, sign, person, or self) CEASING to be actively held / kept-present in an agent's mind-or-regard — the lapse of retention, whereby something that was once held drops out of the holder's active grasp. The root always presupposes prior possession/knowledge of the item and marks its falling-out-of-hold; it does not merely mean "not-attending" (which need not presuppose prior possession) nor "leaving" a physical location.
nsy.plain_explanation: Across every form-family the invariant is a content dropping out of an agent's active mental/relational hold. (1) Plain retention-lapse, form I: "نَسِيَا حُوتَهُمَا" they forgot their fish (18:61), "نَسِيتُ ٱلْحُوتَ" I forgot the fish (18:63:8), Moses "بِمَا نَسِيتُ" what I forgot (18:73), "إِذَا نَسِيتَ" when you forget (18:24), "إِن نَّسِينَآ" if we forget (2:286), and the promise "سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلَا تَنسَىٰٓ" We shall make you recite, so you will not forget (87:6) — here the object is a possessed content (the fish they had, the given recitation) that lapses or is guaranteed not to lapse. (2) Culpable dropping of a known obligation/sign, still form I: "نَسِىَ مَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاهُ" forgot what his hands sent forth (18:57), "نَسُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ" they forgot God (9:67, 59:19), "نَسُوا۟ ٱلذِّكْرَ" forgot the reminder (25:18), "نَسِيتُمْ لِقَآءَ يَوْمِكُمْ" you forgot the meeting of this Day (32:14, 45:34, 7:51), "وَلَا تَنسَ نَصِيبَكَ" do not forget your portion (28:77), "وَلَا تَنسَوُا۟ ٱلْفَضْلَ" do not forget the graciousness between you (2:237), "نَسِىَ خَلْقَهُۥ" forgot his own creation (36:78) — the residue is identical (a held item drops from active regard); context/participants add moral culpability. (3) Divine requital: "ٱلْيَوْمَ نَنسَىٰكُمْ كَمَا نَسِيتُمْ" today We forget you as you forgot (45:34; cf. 7:51 نَنسَىٰهُمْ, 32:14 نَسِينَٰكُمْ, 9:67 فَنَسِيَهُمْ) — God's "forgetting" = ceasing to keep them in beneficent regard, explicitly mirrored on their own nsy by "كَمَا نَسِيتُمْ". (4) Form IV causative (V(IV)): "فَأَنسَىٰهُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ ذِكْرَ رَبِّهِۦ" Satan made him drop remembrance (12:42), "أَنسَىٰنِيهُ إِلَّا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ" none made me forget it but Satan (18:63:11), "أَنسَوْكُمْ ذِكْرِى" made you forget My remembrance (23:110), "فَأَنسَىٰهُمْ ذِكْرَ ٱللَّهِ / أَنفُسَهُمْ" (58:19, 59:19), "يُنسِيَنَّكَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ" (6:68), and abrogation "أَوْ نُنسِهَا" or cause it to be forgotten (2:106) — causer makes a content drop from another's hold. (5) Nominal: "كُنتُ نَسْيًا مَّنسِيًّا" a forgotten thing utterly forgotten (19:23), i.e. the very content that has dropped out; and negated of God "وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ نَسِيًّا" your Lord is never forgetful (19:64), "لَا يَضِلُّ رَبِّى وَلَا يَنسَى" (20:52) — the faculty of dropping-from-hold, denied of God. Every occurrence recovers the same core: something once held ceases to be held.
nsy.strongest_counterexample: The divine requital cases — "ٱلْيَوْمَ نَنسَىٰكُمْ" We forget you today (7:51:10, 45:34:3), "إِنَّا نَسِينَٰكُمْ" (32:14:8), "فَنَسِيَهُمْ" so He forgot them (9:67:15) — are hardest, because the same corpus flatly denies that God forgets: "وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ نَسِيًّا" (19:64) and "لَا يَضِلُّ رَبِّى وَلَا يَنسَى" (20:52). If nsy meant strictly "memory failure," these would be a direct internal contradiction. They reconcile through an internally-attested bridge: each divine "forget" is stamped with "كَمَا نَسِيتُمْ / كَمَا نَسُوا۟" (as you forgot), marking a deliberate talionic mirroring — God ceases to keep them in active beneficent regard exactly as they let Him drop from theirs. The residue "content ceasing to be kept in active hold/regard" survives; only the accidental-vs-deliberate parameter flips, and that flip is supplied by the participant (God) and the explicit mirroring, not by the root. Thus no true contradiction; it is a reconciled extension.

qwm.candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes one image: RISING INTO AND HOLDING AN ERECT, UPRIGHT STANDING — an entity's assumption and sustaining of a vertical/upright orientation (to be, or be made, erect and kept-so). Every branch is a regular extension of this single image: physically stand/rise (I); make-stand → erect / set-up / establish / keep-up (IV); hold-oneself-straight / stay-the-course (X); the quality of the held-upright line = straight/right/correct (mustaqīm, qayyim, aqwam, qiyam, taqwīm); that which keeps standing = subsists / endures / upholds (qāʾim, muqīm, al-Qayyūm, qawwām, qiyām 'mainstay'); the place or event of standing = station / standing / the universal Standing (maqām, qiyām, al-Qiyāmah); and a body constituted to stand-together = a people (qawm).
qwm.plain_explanation: The verb-and-adjective cluster carries the image transparently. Bare I = erect standing/rising: "when they stood up (qāmū)" 18:14; "stand before God devoutly (qūmū)" 2:238; "arise and warn (qum)" 74:2; "the Day people stand before the Lord (yaqūmu)" 83:6; "the Day the Spirit and angels stand in rows" 78:38; and the striking antonym pairings that fix the sense as ERECT posture specifically — "standing (qiyāman) and sitting (quʿūdan) and on their sides" 3:191 & 4:103, "prostrate and standing (qiyāman)" 25:64, "then they are standing (qiyāmun), looking" 39:68. Form IV = cause-to-stand → erect/establish/maintain: literally "he set it (the leaning wall) upright (fa-aqāmahu)" 18:77; then metaphorically "keep up the prayer (aqīmū al-ṣalāt)" (dozens, e.g. 2:3, 2:43, 4:103), "maintain the limits of God (yuqīmā ḥudūd Allāh)" 2:229–230, "keep up the weighing with justice (aqīmū al-wazn)" 55:9, "uphold the Torah and Gospel (aqāmū)" 5:66/5:68, "establish the religion (aqīmū al-dīn)" 42:13, "set your face upright toward the religion (aqim wajhaka)" 10:105/30:30/30:43. Form X = keep straight/steadfast: "remain upright as commanded (fa-staqim)" 11:112, "kept straight on the path (istaqāmū)" 41:30/46:13/72:16, "as long as they stay true (istaqāmū) to you, stay true to them" 9:7. The straightness family is the same erect line abstracted: "straight path (ṣirāṭ mustaqīm)" (very frequent, e.g. 1:6, 6:153), "the straight balance (al-qisṭās al-mustaqīm)" 17:35/26:182, "the upright religion (al-dīn al-qayyim)" 12:40/30:30/9:36, "a straight religion (dīnan qiyaman)" 6:161, the Book "straight, without crookedness (qayyiman)" 18:2, "which is most upright (aqwam)" 17:9, "more upright in speech" 73:6, "best conformation (aḥsan taqwīm)" 95:4. The subsist/endure/uphold branch is internally bridged: God "the Self-Subsisting (al-Qayyūm)" 2:255/3:2/20:111; "standing over (qāʾiman ʿalā) every soul" 13:33; "upholding justice (qāʾiman bi-l-qisṭ)" 3:18; "maintainers over women (qawwāmūna)" 4:34; "steadfast upholders of justice (qawwāmīna bi-l-qisṭ)" 4:135/5:8; "lasting punishment (ʿadhāb muqīm)" 5:37/9:68/11:39/42:45; property "which God made a mainstay (qiyāman) for you" 4:5 and the Kaaba "a mainstay (qiyāman) for people" 5:97; heaven and earth "stand/subsist (taqūma) by His command" 30:25. The place/event branch: "the standing-place of Abraham (maqām Ibrāhīm)" 2:125/3:97, "a praiseworthy station (maqāman maḥmūdan)" 17:79, "who fears the standing before his Lord (maqāma rabbihi)" 55:46/79:40, "two others stand in their stead (maqāmahumā)" 5:107, and the eschatological nominalization "the Day of Standing/Resurrection (yawm al-qiyāmah)" (dozens). Finally qawm "people" (the great bulk of the N tokens, e.g. "the people of Noah" 71:1, "O my people (yā qawmi)" 11:50, "the wrongdoing people (al-qawm al-ẓālimīn)" 5:51) reads as a collective constituted to stand-together as one body — the group aspect of the same "standing/upholding" image that is explicitly attested in qiyāman 'mainstay', qawwāmūn 'upholders', al-Qayyūm and muqīm.
qwm.strongest_counterexample: qawm "a people/folk" (the dominant nominal, e.g. 71:1:5:1 "qawmihi", 11:50:6:2 "yā qawmi", 5:51:21:2 "al-qawm al-ẓālimīn"). Here the erect-standing residue is NOT surface-recoverable in the individual token — "the people of Noah" does not read off "standing." It reconciles only through a derivational/etymological bridge: a qawm is a collective constituted to stand-together as one social body. Crucially, that bridge IS partly attested inside this very corpus, where the same root yields the abstract "standing/upholding/subsisting": qiyāman = a mainstay by which people stand (4:5, 5:97), qawwāmūn = upholders (4:34, 4:135, 5:8), al-Qayyūm = the self-standing sustainer of all (2:255), muqīm = the enduring/standing (5:37). Because qawm nonetheless requires this inferential step rather than surfacing the image directly, it is the single hardest case and the reason the unity is graded MODERATE rather than STRONG — but the residue is neither absent nor contradicted, so it is reconciled, not anomalous.

rbb.candidate_root_contribution: rbb contributes CUSTODIAL MASTERSHIP: the standing of an entity as the party in whose proprietary, sustaining charge another entity is held — one who at once owns/possesses it, sustains and rears it, and authoritatively governs and directs it toward its completion; with a reciprocal passive pole (rabiba) denoting the one so held and reared under that charge. It is a single fused relation "owner–sustainer–governor–rearer," not bare title, not bare command, and not worship-worthiness in the abstract.
rbb.plain_explanation:
Every occurrence is nominal (form N) and instantiates one of five lexeme-types of the doubled root, all reducing to the same charge-relation.

(1) rabb + suffix/idafa (the mass, ~971). The residue surfaces in all its facets. OWNERSHIP/MASTERY over a person: Joseph's house-master "innahu rabbi ahsana mathwaya" (12:23), the king as a servant's rabb "yasqi rabbahu khamran" / "udhkurni inda rabbik" / "irji ila rabbik" (12:41,42,50). SUSTENANCE/PROVISION: the tree yields "bi-idhni rabbiha" (14:25); "ta'adhdhana rabbukum la-in shakartum la-azidannakum" (14:7); the rabb who "yabsutu l-rizqa" (17:30). GOVERNANCE/DIRECTION: "wa-awha rabbuka ila l-nahl" — directing even the bee (16:68); "qada rabbuka alla ta'budu illa iyyah" (17:23); "amru rabbik" as executive command (11:101; 16:33). REARING TO COMPLETION: "yajtabika rabbuka wa-yu'allimuka ... wa-yutimmu ni'matahu alayk" (12:6). The same word names FALSE/CANDIDATE masters when a creature is wrongly treated as the governing charge-holder: "hadha rabbi" of star and sun (6:76-78).

(2) arbab (plural, 4x): the identical relation predicated of illegitimate multiple masters — "alla yattakhidha ba'duna ba'dan arbaban min duni llah" (3:64), angels/prophets as arbab (3:80), rabbis and monks taken as arbab (9:31), "a-arbabun mutafarriqun khayrun am Allahu l-wahid" (12:39). Subtracting plural morphology and the polemical context leaves "masters holding authoritative charge."

(3) rabbaniyy (nisba, 3x): "kunu rabbaniyyina bima kuntum tu'allimuna l-kitab" (3:79); "al-rabbaniyyuna wal-ahbar" charged with guarding/judging by God's book (5:44), and rebuked for failing to restrain wrongdoing (5:63). The -iyy nisba orients the charge-relation two ways at once, both internal to rbb: persons belonging-under/devoted-to the Rabb, and persons who themselves exercise a rearing/teaching charge over others (paired with teaching and guarding scripture).

(4) ribbiyyun (nisba, 1x): "qatala ma'ahu ribbiyyuna kathir" (3:146) — devoted companies fighting alongside a prophet; a nisba to the same base, "those belonging to the Rabb / under the master's cause."

(5) rabaib (1x): "wa-rabaibukumu llati fi hujurikum" (4:23) — step-daughters explicitly glossed by the text as those "in your care/laps." This is the passive pole of the very same relation: the female reared and held in a guardian's custodial charge. It is the decisive internal witness that the root's "rear/sustain" facet is not imported but attested, and that the abstract center genuinely fuses governance with rearing.

Across all five, subtract morphology, construction, participants and context and the same non-empty invariant remains: X stands in a proprietary-sustaining-governing charge over Y (or, passively, Y is held/reared under X).
rbb.strongest_counterexample: rabaib at 4:23:20:2 ("wa-rabaibukumu llati fi hujurikum"). It is hardest because its referent is the OBJECT of the charge (a step-daughter), not the charge-HOLDER (master/lord) that every other occurrence names; on a naive gloss "rbb = lord" it looks contradicted (a step-daughter is not a lord). It reconciles cleanly by FORM-layer subtraction: rabiba is a fa'ila form with passive orientation, the correlative pole of the same rbb relation — "the one reared and held in custodial charge." The residue "custodial-rearing charge" is fully present; only the diathesis (agent vs patient of the relation) flips, which is morphology, not a root contradiction. The verse's own gloss "fi hujurikum" ("in your care") makes the charge-relation surface-explicit. Far from breaking the unity, this occurrence supplies the internal bridge proving the "rear/sustain" facet of the abstract center.

rjm.candidate_root_contribution: The forcible propulsion of hard projectiles at a target — a directed hurling/pelting whose function is to strike, batter, and thereby drive off, expel, or bring down that target.
rjm.plain_explanation: Across every occurrence the root contributes the image of pelting: hard objects hurled AT a target to strike and repel it. (1) The finite verbs are all literal stoning threats — "we would have stoned you" (11:91 لَرَجَمْنَٰكَ), "they will stone you" (18:20 يَرْجُمُوكُمْ), "I will surely stone you" (19:46 لَأَرْجُمَنَّكَ), "we will surely stone you" (36:18 لَنَرْجُمَنَّكُمْ), "that you stone me" (44:20 تَرْجُمُونِ). Here the pelting-to-drive-off/kill is on the surface. (2) The passive participle marjūmīn (26:116, "you will be among the pelted ones") is the same act viewed from the target. (3) rujūm (67:5) names the projectiles themselves: the sky's lamps are "made rujūm FOR the devils" — objects hurled to drive off the shayāṭīn; this verse is the internal keystone tying the projectile sense to the shayṭān. (4) The epithet rajīm — Iblīs told "you are rajīm" then expelled (15:34, 38:77), and "the rajīm Satan" (15:17, 16:98, 3:36, 81:25) — is exactly the passive "pelted/driven-off, hence outcast" one, bridged internally by 67:5's rujūm-for-devils. (5) rajm bi-l-ghayb (18:22, guessing the sleepers' number) is the same hurl-at-a-target act with the target unseen: casting conjecture blindly "at the hidden." Subtracting form, construction, participants and context, the invariant left is: cast hard things at a target to strike and drive it away.
rjm.strongest_counterexample: 18:22 رَجْمًۢا بِٱلْغَيْبِ ("rajm at the unseen," i.e. guessing the number of the Sleepers). It contains no stones and no expulsion, so it looks like a pure speech-act. It reconciles because the root still supplies the throwing/casting act: the speakers are hurling assertions AT a target they cannot see, so the projectile is verbal and the "unseen" is the missing target — the very feature (blind, aimless casting) that distinguishes it from informed speech. The construction bi-l-ghayb, not the root, adds "at the hidden"; strip it and the recoverable residue is still "casting [something] at [a target]." A close runner-up is the rajīm epithet (e.g. 15:34, 3:36): on the surface it reads as static "accursed/outcast," but 67:5 supplies the internal bridge — devils are the standing objects of rujūm (hurled projectiles) — so rajīm = "the pelted-and-thereby-driven-off one," not an unrelated sense of cursing.

rsw.candidate_root_contribution: Firm, weighted anchoring — the condition or act of being made to settle immovably in place by being grounded/moored to a fixed point, so that the thing neither drifts, sways, nor moves off its position.
rsw.plain_explanation: Across all 14 occurrences the root contributes one thing: fixedness-by-anchoring. (1) The dominant cluster is the plural participle رَوَاسِيَ / رَوَاسِيْ "firmly-anchored ones" = mountains, used 9 times (13:3, 15:19, 16:15, 21:31, 27:61, 31:10, 41:10, 50:7, 77:27). Their function is spelled out repeatedly: they are cast/placed "into the earth" أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ — "lest it sway with you" (16:15, 21:31, 31:10). The residue here is not merely "big rock" but "the anchoring element that holds the earth immovable." (2) 34:13 رَّاسِيَاتٍ describes cauldrons that are fixed/immovable in place (too heavy to be moved), the same fixedness applied to a different object. (3) 79:32 the causative verb أَرْسَاهَا "He anchored them" (the mountains) — the verbal expression of the same firm-fixing act. (4) The verbal-noun cluster مُرْسَىٰ (form IV, N(IV)): in 11:41 the ship's بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ مَجْرَاهَا وَمُرْسَاهَا contrasts "its running/coursing" (مجرى) with "its mooring/coming-to-rest" (مرسى) — the point/act at which a moving vessel is brought to firm rest. In 79:42 and 7:187 مُرْسَاهَا asks of the Hour "when is its mursā" — its coming-to-its-fixed-appointed-settling, i.e. its being brought to its determinate, unmovable point of realization. In every case what rsw supplies is the same abstract core: coming/being brought to a firmly-fixed, non-drifting settledness anchored to a point.
rsw.strongest_counterexample: 79:42:5:1 (= 7:187:5:1) مُرْسَىٰهَا applied to the Hour. This is the only clearly non-spatial occurrence: the Hour cannot be physically "moored." It reconciles through an internally-attested bridge: the very same form N(IV) مُرْسَى in 11:41 denotes a ship's coming-to-rest/mooring point, explicitly paired against its motion (مجرى "running"). Extending that, the Hour's مرسى is its being brought to its fixed, appointed point of settled realization — the moment at which the presently "running/pending" event is anchored to its determinate arrival. The fixedness-to-a-determinate-point residue is thus recoverable, though via metaphorical (spatial→temporal) extension.

sbl.candidate_root_contribution: The root sbl contributes the notion of a WAY: a determinate, extended, traversable course/route that links a mover to a destination — something one goes along, is led along, opens, straightens, follows, or is barred from — and, by natural extension of the same conduit-image, the open avenue or means by which one proceeds toward an outcome. The root supplies only the traversable-course itself; it is normatively neutral (the way's rightness or wrongness, its physical vs. figurative destination, and its direction are all added by the genitive/preposition/context, not by sbl).
sbl.plain_explanation: Every one of the 176 tokens is the substantive سبيل/سبل. The most transparent occurrences anchor the core as a concrete traversable route: God places rivers "and ways" (سبلا) in the earth so people may find their way (16:15), makes "ways" for them in it (20:53, 43:10), broad mountain passes as ways (فجاجا سبلا 21:31, 71:20); the bee is told to travel "the ways of your Lord" (سبل ربك 16:69); the lost fish "took its way into the sea" (اتخذ سبيله في البحر 18:61, 18:63); Lot's ruined town lies "by a way still standing" (لبسبيل مقيم 15:76). Here sbl = physical road/route, undeniably a traversable course. From this concrete anchor the same image extends, with the destination becoming a goal or standard rather than a place: 'the way' one is guided to (هديناه السبيل 76:3; يهدي السبيل 33:4; ثم السبيل يسّره 80:20), the way of right-conduct vs. the way of error (سبيل الرشد / سبيل الغي 7:146; سبيل الرشاد 40:38), the even/middle way (سواء السبيل 2:108, 5:12). Crucially the root stays normatively neutral: it attaches equally to the way of God (فى سبيل الله, dozens of times), the way of the criminals (سبيل المجرمين 6:55), of the corrupters (سبيل المفسدين 7:142), and 'the ways' one is warned NOT to follow (لا تتبعوا السبل 6:153) — so 'rightness' is not in sbl but in the genitive. The dense 'fī sabīl Allāh' frame (fighting 2:190, spending 2:195, migrating 4:100, striving 9:20) reads as motion/effort ALONG God's course. The negative-motion frame — barring from the way (صدوا عن سبيل الله 16:88), leading astray from it (ليضل عن سبيله 14:30), going astray from it (ضل عن سبيله 53:30) — presupposes exactly a course that can be traversed or diverted from. The traveler is 'son of the way' (ابن السبيل 2:177, 9:60) and the one merely 'crossing a way' (عابر سبيل 4:43) — persons defined by being on the road. Finally the 'means/recourse' cluster keeps the same conduit-image with an abstract terminus: 'is there any way OUT?' (هل الى خروج من سبيل 40:11), 'any way of return?' (الى مرد من سبيل 42:44), 'no way [of recourse]' (فما له من سبيل 42:46), and the liability idiom 'no way [of blame] against them / the way is against the wrongdoers' (ما عليهم من سبيل 42:41; السبيل على الذين 42:42; 3:75; 9:91,93), 'God will not grant the disbelievers a way over the believers' (سبيلا 4:141) — each is an avenue/route by which action or outcome may proceed. Across every family the invariant left after subtraction is 'a traversable course toward a terminus'.
sbl.strongest_counterexample: The hardest cluster is the abstract liability/recourse idiom, especially 42:42 (إِنَّمَا ٱلسَّبِيلُ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يَظْلِمُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ — 'the sabīl is only against those who wrong people') and 3:75 (لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِى ٱلْأُمِّيِّـۧنَ سَبِيلٌ — 'there is no sabīl against us regarding the gentiles'), plus 4:141 (a sabīl 'over' the believers) and 4:34 (do not seek a sabīl 'against' them). Here sabīl denotes grounds/entitlement-to-proceed, with no physical road and an abstract terminus (blame, dominance). It reconciles because the construction ʿalā/against + sabīl preserves the exact conduit-structure: an OPEN AVENUE/ROUTE by which action may proceed toward someone — negated ('no route of claim exists') or asserted ('the route of liability lies against the wrongdoers'). The internal bridge is attested within the same idiom-space: 40:11 'is there any way OUT (min sabīl)?' is a near-literal route-of-egress, and 42:44 'any way of RETURN' the same; the liability cases are just that route-to-outcome with the outcome being an act rather than a place. So the traversable-course image is recoverable, not forced.

tbE.candidate_root_contribution: The root places one entity in the wake/track of another that precedes it, such that the trailing entity comes-behind-and-along the course of the leading reference. The subject (or the entity made-to-trail) is positioned AFTER a preceding reference-point and conforms its motion/sequence/course to it: a "going-after / coming-behind-in-the-track-of." Direction is fixed — the follower is behind, the followed goes before and sets the track.
tbE.plain_explanation: Across all form-families the invariant is a leading reference X ahead and a trailing entity Y behind that moves in X's wake. (1) LITERAL MOTION/PURSUIT: Pharaoh "trailed after" the Israelites (10:90:5:2 fa-atbaʿahum; 20:78:1:2), the shooting-star "pursues/trails" the eavesdropping devil (15:18:5:2; 37:10:5:2 fa-atbaʿahu shihāb), "follow their backs/tracks" (15:65:6:2 wa-ttabiʿ adbārahum), "he took-to a route" (18:85:1:2/89/92 atbaʿa sababan), "you will be pursued" (26:52; 44:23 muttabaʿūn). (2) SEQUENCE/SUCCESSION: "the following blast trails it" (79:7:1:1 tatbaʿuhā al-rādifah), "We made the later ones follow" (77:17:2:1), "We made some follow others" one after another (23:44:11:2), two "consecutive/successive" months (4:92 & 58:4 mutatābiʿayn, form VI reciprocal = one-behind-another). (3) APPENDING/TRAILING A CONSEQUENCE (form IV causative): "do not follow-up (attach after) your spending with reproach" (2:262:9:1 yutbiʿūna...mannan), "charity that injury follows" (2:263:7:1 yatbaʿuhā adhan), "We made a curse trail them in this world" (11:60; 11:99; 28:42:1:2 atbaʿnāhum laʿnatan). (4) ALLEGIANCE / DISCIPLESHIP / ADHERENCE (the dominant form VIII cluster): fall in behind the Messenger (2:143:22:1; 7:157), the revelation (10:109; 6:106:1:1 ittabiʿ mā ūḥiya), guidance (2:38:10:1 tabiʿa hudāya; 20:123), Abraham's creed (16:123; 3:95), God's good-pleasure (5:16; 3:174) — versus falling in behind desires (hawā: 18:28; 25... 47:14; 38:26), conjecture (10:36; 53:23 yattabiʿūna illā al-ẓanna), Satan's "footsteps" (khuṭuwāt 2:168; 6:142; 24:21), a "path" (sabīl 31:15; ṣirāṭ 43:61). "Those who were-followed" (leaders) vs "those who followed" (2:166-167 uttubiʿū / ittabaʿū) makes the leader/trailer polarity explicit. (5) AGENTIVE NOUNS: "followers/dependents" (14:21; 40:47 tabaʿan), household "attendants" who trail (24:31 al-tābiʿīn), a "pursuer/claimant" who comes after to demand redress (17:69:22:1 tabīʿan). In every case, subtracting form and context leaves the same residue: Y in the track of a preceding X.
tbE.strongest_counterexample: The form-IV "append-after" cases where both terms are abstract and static — 2:262:9:1 "do not follow-up (yutbiʿūna) what you spent with reproach (mannan)" and 2:263:7:1 "charity that injury (adhan) follows." Here the "leading" element (the act of spending) is not itself moving and the "trailer" (reproach/injury) is not an agent tracking a path. Yet the residue survives cleanly: Y is placed AFTER X in sequence and issues from/attaches to it — the reproach is dispatched to come in the wake of the gift. This is the same directional "coming-after" seen literally in 79:7 (one blast trailing another) and 23:44 (messengers sent one-after-another), only with an abstract trailer. It reconciles without forcing: the before/after ordering and the wake-relation are intact.

vwy.candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes DURATIVE STAYING / SETTLED RESIDENCE — the notion of abiding, lodging, or taking up (and remaining in) occupancy of a place. Its invariant is the act of remaining-resident somewhere, not merely being located there momentarily; what derives from it is either the place-of-such-staying or the one-who-so-stays.
vwy.plain_explanation: Every occurrence is nominal (form_inventory: N ×14) and every token but one is the ism-makān مَثْوَى ("place of staying/abiding, lodging, abode"); the single non-مَثْوَى token is the active participle ثَاوِيًا "one residing/dwelling" (28:45). Subtracting those morphological wrappers leaves one shared verbal kernel: to stay/reside/lodge in a place over time. Concrete evidence across families: (1) NARRATIVE/LODGING family — 12:21 "أَكْرِمِى مَثْوَىٰهُ" (make honorable his lodging/place-of-stay, of Joseph taken into the Egyptian's house) and 12:23 "أَحْسَنَ مَثْوَاىَ" (he made good my residence/lodging); here مَثْوَى is the domestic place where one is settled to stay. (2) PARTICIPLE family — 28:45 "وَمَا كُنتَ ثَاوِيًا فِىٓ أَهْلِ مَدْيَنَ" (you were not a resident/dweller among the people of Midyan): pure durative residence with no place-noun morphology, exposing the verbal residue "to reside" directly. (3) ESCHATOLOGICAL family (the large cluster: 16:29; 29:68; 39:32; 39:60; 39:72; 3:151; 40:76; 41:24; 47:12; 6:128; and the general 47:19) — Hell/the Fire as "مَثْوَى" of the arrogant/wrongdoers/disbelievers, i.e. the place where they permanently reside; this is reinforced construction-internally by the recurring "خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا" (abiding therein) in 16:29, 39:72, 40:76, 6:128, which spells out precisely the staying/remaining that مَثْوَى names as a locus. Whether the stay is honorable lodging (Joseph), neutral residence (Midyan, "مَثْوَىٰكُمْ" 47:19) or dreadful eternal confinement (Hell), the root residue is identical: settled remaining-in-place.
vwy.strongest_counterexample: The hardest cases are 12:21 "أَكْرِمِى مَثْوَىٰهُ" and 12:23 "أَحْسَنَ مَثْوَاىَ," where مَثْوَى can be felt as "treatment/hospitality" rather than a physical spot, which risks drifting the root toward an abstract "manner of reception." It reconciles cleanly: even there مَثْوَى denotes the place-and-conditions of Joseph's staying in the household (he was literally settled to reside there — "عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَنفَعَنَآ أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُۥ وَلَدًا"), so the residue "settled residence/lodging" is intact; "honor his lodging" = treat-well the residence in which he abides. The abstraction is an extension of, not a departure from, durative residence, and it stays within the same morphological form as the eschatological tokens, so no separate sense is needed.

w*r.candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes RELINQUISHMENT-INTO-REMAINING: the agent's withdrawal of holding/acting-upon/attending-to an object, such that the object is simply left standing in whatever state it is in, apart from the agent, without further intervention. It marks non-retention (letting-remain / letting-be), not motion, seizure, or destruction; direction is always agent-releases → object-persists-on-its-own.
w*r.plain_explanation:
Every one of the 45 tokens is the same defective Form-I verb (ذَرْ / يَذَرُ / نَذَرُ / تَذَرُونَ etc.) and in each the residue "release the object to remain as it is" is directly recoverable, across five observable sense-clusters that differ only by object and context:

(1) Leave persons in their present state / to their own devices — the object stays put and the agent ceases involvement: 10:11 "فَنَذَرُ ٱلَّذِينَ ... فِى طُغْيَٰنِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ" (leave them wandering in their transgression), 6:110, 7:186 (same frame), 15:3 "ذَرْهُمْ يَأْكُلُوا۟", 23:54 "فَذَرْهُمْ فِى غَمْرَتِهِمْ", 43:83/70:42/52:45 "فَذَرْهُمْ ... حَتَّىٰ يُلَٰقُوا۟", 6:91 "ذَرْهُمْ فِى خَوْضِهِمْ", 6:112/6:137 "فَذَرْهُمْ وَمَا يَفْتَرُونَ", 6:70/7:180 "ذَرِ/ذَرُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ ...", 3:179 "لِيَذَرَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَىٰ مَآ أَنتُمْ عَلَيْهِ" (leave-in-that-state, negated). Requests to "leave me alone with X" are the same withdrawal, addressee-directed: 73:11 "وَذَرْنِى وَٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ", 74:11 "ذَرْنِى وَمَنْ خَلَقْتُ", 68:44 "فَذَرْنِى وَمَن يُكَذِّبُ"; and permission-to-act framings 40:26 "ذَرُونِىٓ أَقْتُلْ" (leave me [free] to kill), 48:15 "ذَرُونَا نَتَّبِعْكُمْ", 9:86 "ذَرْنَا نَكُن مَّعَ ٱلْقَٰعِدِينَ" — in each the speaker asks to be released/left so as to remain in a chosen state or act.

(2) Leave an object standing in a specified physical state: 11:64/7:73 "فَذَرُوهَا تَأْكُلْ فِىٓ أَرْضِ ٱللَّهِ" (leave the she-camel to graze), 12:47 "فَذَرُوهُ فِى سُنۢبُلِهِ" (leave the grain in its ear), 20:106 "فَيَذَرُهَا قَاعًا صَفْصَفًا" (leave it a level plain), 4:129 "فَتَذَرُوهَا كَٱلْمُعَلَّقَةِ" (leave her as one suspended). Object clearly persists in a state after the agent stops acting.

(3) Give up / cease engaging with a practice or thing (directive to stop holding it): 2:278 "وَذَرُوا۟ مَا بَقِىَ مِنَ ٱلرِّبَوٰٓا۟", 62:9 "وَذَرُوا۟ ٱلْبَيْعَ", 6:120 "وَذَرُوا۟ ظَٰهِرَ ٱلْإِثْمِ وَبَاطِنَهُ".

(4) Culpable forsaking/neglect (same residue; the negative valence is supplied by the object + context, not the root): 26:166 "وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُم", 37:125 "وَتَذَرُونَ أَحْسَنَ ٱلْخَٰلِقِينَ", 7:70 "وَنَذَرَ مَا كَانَ يَعْبُدُ ءَابَآؤُنَا", 71:23 (×2) "لَا تَذَرُنَّ ءَالِهَتَكُمْ ... وَدًّا", 75:21 "وَتَذَرُونَ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةَ", 76:27 "وَيَذَرُونَ وَرَآءَهُمْ يَوْمًا ثَقِيلًا". Note 71:23 and 37:125 are the SAME verb whose object is idols/God — proving the valence is not in the root.

(5) Leave-behind by death / leave-remaining, incl. negated "leave nothing": 2:234 & 2:240 "وَيَذَرُونَ أَزْوَٰجًا" (leave surviving wives). Survival/sparing: 21:89 "لَا تَذَرْنِى فَرْدًا" (do not leave me solitary), 71:26 "لَا تَذَرْ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ ... دَيَّارًا" (do not leave a single dweller), 71:27 "إِن تَذَرْهُمْ يُضِلُّوا۟", 7:127 (×2) "أَتَذَرُ مُوسَىٰ ... وَيَذَرَكَ وَءَالِهَتَكَ" (will you leave Moses free... and he leave/abandon you). The apparent "destruction" tokens are simply this residue under negation — nothing is let-remain: 51:42 "مَا تَذَرُ مِن شَىْءٍ أَتَتْ عَلَيْهِ" (leaves nothing it strikes), 74:28 "لَا تُبْقِى وَلَا تَذَرُ" (spares not, leaves not). Here 'leaving/remaining' is exactly what is denied, confirming the residue by its negation.
w*r.strongest_counterexample: 51:42 "مَا تَذَرُ مِن شَىْءٍ أَتَتْ عَلَيْهِ إِلَّا جَعَلَتْهُ كَٱلرَّمِيمِ" and 74:28 "لَا تُبْقِى وَلَا تَذَرُ" appear opposite to the core, since the salient event is total DESTRUCTION, not gentle leaving. They reconcile cleanly under layer-subtraction: the verb here is NEGATED, and what is negated is precisely "letting-remain" — the wind/Saqar lets nothing persist. The destruction is contributed by the surrounding clause (جَعَلَتْهُ كَٱلرَّمِيمِ) and by the parallel لَا تُبْقِى; the root still means only "leave-to-remain," now denied. Thus the hardest cases actually corroborate the residue by exhibiting its negation.

xrj.candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes EGRESS: the passage of an entity from within a bounding/containing locus to the outside of it — a boundary-crossing whose determinate direction is interior→exterior ("coming, or being brought, to be outside of what previously held it"). The root supplies only the out-directed transition plus the implied prior enclosure/source; whether the entity moves of itself, is driven out by an agent, or is procured out is a matter of FORM (I intransitive egress; IV causative "bring/drive/produce out"; X "extract, draw out"), and what the enclosure is (womb, earth, home, grave, darkness, concealment, a container) is a matter of CONTEXT.
xrj.plain_explanation: Across every form-family the same "out-of-an-interior" vector recurs. Form I (V) is the entity itself crossing out: kharaja minhaa "he went out of it" (28:21); takhruju min afwaahihim, words "come out of their mouths" (18:5); yakhruju min butuunihaa sharaab, drink "comes out of their bellies" (16:69); yakhruju min bayni s-sulb (86:7, semen); yakhrujuuna mina l-ajdaath, they "come out of the graves" (70:43); kharajuu min diyaarihim (2:243, 8:47). Form IV (V(IV)) is the causative — an agent effects that same egress of an object: akhrajakum min butuuni ummahaatikum "brought you out of your mothers' wombs" (16:78); fa-akhraja bihi mina th-thamaraat "brought forth fruits by it [water]" (2:22, 14:32, 6:99, 7:57); yukhriju l-hayya mina l-mayyit "brings the living out of the dead" (6:95, 10:31, 30:19, 3:27); akhrijuuhum min qaryatikum "drive them out of your town" (7:82, 27:56); yukhrijuhum mina z-zulumaati ila n-nuur "brings them out of darkness into light" (2:257, 5:16, 14:1, 33:43, 57:9, 65:11). Form X (V(X)) profiles procuring/effecting the egress = extract: istakhrajahaa min wiʿaaʾi akhiihi "drew it out of his brother's bag" (12:76); tastakhrijuu minhu hilyah "extract ornaments from it" (16:14, 35:12); yastakhrijaa kanzahumaa "bring out their treasure" (18:82). The nominals nominalize the same event: khuruuj / yawmu l-khuruuj "the coming-forth" (50:42, 40:11, 9:46, 9:83); makhraj "a way out" (65:2) and makhraja sidqin "a true bringing-out" (17:80); ikhraaj "the driving-out/expulsion" (2:217, 2:240, 2:85, 9:13, 60:9); active participles mukhrij "one who brings out" (2:72, 6:95, 9:64) and passive mukhraj/mukhrajuun "one(s) brought out" (15:48, 23:35, 26:167, 27:67, 71:18); and the go-forth-participle khaarijiin "coming out" (2:167, 5:37, 6:122). Even the abstract senses stay inside the same interior→exterior frame: yukhriju l-khabʾ "brings out the hidden" (27:25), mukhrijun maa taktumuun / maa tahdharuun "brings out [into the open] what you conceal/dread" (2:72, 9:64), yukhrij adghaanahum "brings out their [hidden] rancor" (47:29, 47:37) — all "the concealed interior brought to the exterior."
xrj.strongest_counterexample: The nominal kharj / kharaaj "tribute, levy, yield" (18:94:13:1 "shall we assign you a kharj?"; 23:72:3:1 and 23:72:4:2 "do you ask them a kharj? — but the kharaaj of your Lord is better"). On the surface this is a payment/return, not a spatial exit. It reconciles as the nominalization of the productive branch of egress: kharaaj is "that which is issued/rendered forth" — a yield or outlay brought out from a source. The bridge is internally attested in this very packet, where God's repeatedly "brings forth" (akhraja) provision, fruit, grain and pasture out of the earth (2:22, 6:99, 7:57, 79:31, 87:4); 23:72 explicitly contrasts a human-demanded kharj with "the kharaaj of your Lord [who] is the best of providers" — i.e., the divinely-issued-forth provision. So kharj/kharaaj = the thing rendered/produced-out, which keeps the interior→exterior residue at the nominal level. It is the single occurrence-set where the residue is not surface-spatial and needs this nominalizing bridge.

zyn.candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes the notion of ENDOWING-WITH-ATTRACTIVE-APPEARANCE: the imparting or presence of an added, ornamental layer of appeal that renders a thing beautiful, pleasing, and desirable to a perceiver. The residue is not intrinsic goodness but the applied/perceptible attractiveness — the "decked-out, made-to-look-appealing" surface — whether that surface is literal decoration or the cognitive semblance of appeal.
zyn.plain_explanation: Three form-families all reduce to one core. (1) The noun zīnah names the attractive/decorative appearance itself or the objects functioning as such: jewelry and finery (zīnat al-qawm 20:87; women's zīnah 24:31 x3, 24:60; Qārūn going out fī zīnatihi 28:79), fine attire at the mosque (7:31), the "adornment God brought forth" (7:32), horses/mules as zīnah (16:8), the earth's decorative surface (18:7), the day of festival-finery (yawm al-zīnah 20:59), the stars as the sky's zīnah (37:6:5), and the appealing surface of worldly life (11:15, 18:28, 18:46, 28:60, 33:28, 57:20, 10:88 with amwāl). In every case the word marks something valued for its attractive show. (2) The V(II) causative zayyana X (li-Y) = 'make X appear beautiful/appealing to Y.' With a physical object this is genuine embellishment: zayyannā al-samā' bi-maṣābīḥ / bi-zīnati l-kawākib (37:6, 41:12, 67:5, 50:6) and zayyannāhā li-l-nāẓirīn (15:16) — adorned FOR the beholders. With deeds/worldly life/an evil act as object it is the cognitive counterpart: things rendered appealing so the perceiver finds them beautiful — zuyyina li-lladhīna kafarū l-ḥayātu l-dunyā (2:212); zayyana lahumu l-shayṭānu aʿmālahum (8:48, 16:63, 27:24, 29:38, 6:43); zuyyina lahum sūʾu aʿmālihim / sūʾu ʿamalihi (9:37, 35:8, 40:37, 47:14). Verse 35:8 makes the residue explicit and self-documenting: 'afaman zuyyina lahū sūʾu ʿamalihi fa-raʾāhu ḥasanan — the evil deed is zuyyina and THEREBY he SEES it as good; i.e., zyn supplies the attractive appearance that produces the perception of goodness. (3) The single V(V) izzayyanat (10:24) is the reflexive/middle: the earth 'took on its adornment (zukhruf) and decked itself out' — became-attractive. Subtracting the causative morphology (zayyana), the beneficiary/dative frame (li- = 'appealing TO whom'), the reflexive frame (izzayyanat = 'became adorned'), and the nominal frame (zīnah = the adornment as thing), the constant left in all 46 is: attractive, ornamental appeal imparted to / present on / perceived in something.
zyn.strongest_counterexample: 49:7 — wa-zayyanahū fī qulūbikum, of ÎMÂN (faith), paired with ḥabbaba ('endeared'). This is the hardest because it is (i) positive-valenced, (ii) internal/cognitive rather than visual decoration, and (iii) about a true good, so one might fear the root here means merely 'endear/make-beloved' rather than 'attractive appearance.' It reconciles cleanly: the residue is 'rendered appealing/attractive,' and faith is here made appealing to the hearts — the same operation as making deeds appealing (8:48) or the sky appealing to beholders (15:16), only with a good object and internal field. The visual→cognitive extension is not an ad hoc rescue: it is internally bridged, since the corpus attests BOTH the overtly visual pole (zayyannāhā li-l-nāẓirīn, 'for the beholders,' 15:16) and the overtly internal pole (zuyyina dhālika fī qulūbikum, 48:12) using the identical form, so 'appeal to a perceiver' is the shared abstract that spans eye and heart.

$yA.candidate_root_contribution: UNRESOLVED: the Quran-internal evidence has a thing/entity family and a willing/choosing family, but does not itself demonstrate a non-circular bridge between them.
$yA.plain_explanation: All 519 confirmed occurrences divide cleanly into 283 noun tokens denoting a thing or particular and 236 verb tokens denoting willing. Both families are internally stable, yet a proposed bridge such as 'a determinate possibility brought into view' merely restates both families at a level too broad to distinguish this root.
$yA.strongest_counterexample: The noun in 10:36 denotes an indefinite thing, while the verb in 10:107 denotes divine willing; neither verse entails the other semantic family.

ArD.candidate_root_contribution: the terrestrial ground or earth-domain, the created lower spatial field on which creatures dwell and events occur
ArD.plain_explanation: All 461 occurrences are noun uses of earth, land, or ground. Recurrent heaven-earth contrasts establish the terrestrial domain, while travel, settlement, growth, corruption, inheritance, and prostration contexts profile it as traversable and inhabited ground.
ArD.strongest_counterexample: Territorial uses such as inheritance of a specific land narrow the referent, but retain the same ground-domain contribution.

mvl.candidate_root_contribution: correspondence through a comparable configuration, by which one case, form, or pattern can stand alongside another
mvl.plain_explanation: The 169 occurrences cover likeness, comparable kind, parable/example, exemplary pattern, and one taking of a human form. Across them the stable residue is not identity but structured correspondence that makes comparison or representation possible.
mvl.strongest_counterexample: 19:17 uses Form V for the spirit appearing as a well-proportioned human, not for an explicit verbal comparison.

qlb.candidate_root_contribution: turning or reorientation between faces, directions, or states; the heart is profiled as the inner center susceptible to such orientation
qlb.plain_explanation: The 168 occurrences span hearts, physical turning, return, reversal, fluctuation, and destination. Explicit heart-turning at 24:37 and repeated descriptions of hearts being sealed, deviated, or stabilized give an internal bridge between the organ/inner center and reorientation.
qlb.strongest_counterexample: The 132 heart nouns often lack overt motion, so the orienting/turnable-center reading depends on the internally explicit bridge in 24:37 and related heart-state changes.

swA.candidate_root_contribution: an adverse or worsening quality by which a condition, act, outcome, or exposed thing is experienced or judged as bad
swA.plain_explanation: Across 167 occurrences, noun and adjective families denote evil, bad acts, harms, shameful exposure, or an adverse outcome; base verbs say a state is bad or someone is distressed, and Form IV produces or embodies badness.
swA.strongest_counterexample: The exposed-private-parts family is concrete and referential, but the verses frame exposure as shameful/adverse, preserving the negative-quality residue.

ysr.candidate_root_contribution: low obstruction or ready attainability, yielding ease, facilitation, or what is readily available
ysr.plain_explanation: Forty-one of 44 occurrences directly instantiate ease, small burden, facilitation, or ready availability across nouns, adjectives, and Forms II/V/X. The three maysir gambling occurrences form a stable lexical family, but the Quran does not internally establish their link to low obstruction.
ysr.strongest_counterexample: The maysir tokens in 2:219, 5:90, and 5:91 denote gambling and do not state that ease or ready acquisition is their root contribution.

fSl.candidate_root_contribution: drawing or making a decisive boundary that separates components and thereby renders a matter distinct, detailed, or settled
fSl.plain_explanation: The 43 occurrences move from separating and judgment to detailed exposition and decisive speech. Separation supplies the boundary; Form II repeatedly makes internal distinctions explicit; judgment and 'word of decision' settle between alternatives.
fSl.strongest_counterexample: Tafsil in exposition is not physical separation, yet it visibly partitions content into distinct intelligible elements.

jwb.candidate_root_contribution: meeting an address, call, or demand with a directed answering response
jwb.plain_explanation: Forty-two occurrences form a coherent answer/respond family across jawāb and Forms IV/X. The remaining base verb at 89:9 means hewing rock in the valley; the Quran supplies no internal bridge from answering to cutting through stone.
jwb.strongest_counterexample: 89:9:3:1 describes Thamud hewing rock, with no speech act or call-response relation.

trk.candidate_root_contribution: ceasing to retain or accompany something, so that it is left, abandoned, spared, or left behind
trk.plain_explanation: All 43 occurrences present an agent not continuing to hold, practice, accompany, destroy, or carry something. Context determines whether the remainder is abandonment, preservation, inheritance, or residue.
trk.strongest_counterexample: Leaving descendants or an inheritance can look like positive bequeathal, but it still profiles what remains when the prior holder departs.

Sdd.candidate_root_contribution: placing or undergoing an obstruction that turns movement, access, or response away from its course
Sdd.plain_explanation: Forty-one of 42 occurrences are verbs or action nouns of hindering, turning away, being barred, or a blocking structure. The adjective/noun sadid at 14:16 denotes a hellish fluid and does not expose obstruction or turning-away in its verse.
Sdd.strongest_counterexample: 14:16:7:1 describes water called sadid; the occurrence has no path, barrier, or redirection relation.

wlj.candidate_root_contribution: passing or causing passage across an outside/inside boundary into an interior domain
wlj.plain_explanation: Thirteen verbs describe entering the earth or interpenetration of night and day; the one walija noun denotes a privileged intimate taken into one's inner circle. The latter is a social extension of interior access.
wlj.strongest_counterexample: 9:16 uses walija for an intimate rather than physical entry, so the inside-access bridge is metaphorical.

$hw.candidate_root_contribution: an appetite that draws the self toward a desired object or experience
$hw.plain_explanation: All 13 occurrences concern what persons or souls crave, whether the object is lawful, unlawful, worldly, or eschatological. Verbs profile directed desiring; nouns profile the appetite or its pursued objects.
$hw.strongest_counterexample: Paradisal uses are positive while following appetites can be condemned; the polarity shift confirms that the root supplies appetite, not moral judgment.

Dyq.candidate_root_contribution: constriction: reduced room or capacity, physically, circumstantially, or inwardly
Dyq.plain_explanation: All 13 occurrences express narrow space, constrained circumstances, tightened provision, or inward constriction of breast. Form II causes constriction; nouns/adjectives name the constrained state or place.
Dyq.strongest_counterexample: Emotional constriction of the breast is non-spatial, but the corpus repeatedly frames distress through the explicit container term sadr, preserving reduced inner room.

Hlf.candidate_root_contribution: binding one's assertion by an invoked oath
Hlf.plain_explanation: All 13 occurrences are acts of swearing or the habitual swearer. Truth or falsehood belongs to the asserted content; the root supplies oath-binding performance.
Hlf.strongest_counterexample: Many oaths are knowingly false, but falsity affects content rather than whether the speaker binds the assertion with an oath.

Sgr.candidate_root_contribution: reduction or lowness on a scale of magnitude or standing
Sgr.plain_explanation: Seven occurrences concern small size, age, or amount; six concern abasement or lowered status. The shared scale relation is being below a comparator in magnitude or standing.
Sgr.strongest_counterexample: Saghar and saghirun describe humiliation rather than small dimensions; explicit contrasts with arrogance and dignity support a rank-scale extension.

Ezr.candidate_root_contribution: actively reinforcing and upholding another so that the person or mission stands supported
Ezr.plain_explanation: All three Form II occurrences coordinate reinforcing messengers or the Messenger with believing, honoring, obeying, and glorifying. The repeated participant pattern supports active upholding rather than generic praise.
Ezr.strongest_counterexample: 48:9 coordinates ta'zir with tawqir, creating a risk that the root merely means honor; coordination suggests related but non-identical contributions.

Hdq.candidate_root_contribution: a cultivated garden-space characterized in the Quran by planted growth and abundance
Hdq.plain_explanation: All three occurrences are the plural hada'iq: delightful gardens, gardens and grapes, and dense gardens. The corpus establishes the referential garden class but offers no verbs or contrasts from which to extract a deeper abstract mechanism.
Hdq.strongest_counterexample: Because every token is the same plural noun, universal presence may reflect lexical repetition rather than a tested derivational core.

Hlq.candidate_root_contribution: UNRESOLVED: shaving/removing hair and the throat are both clear, but their proposed circular-boundary bridge is not demonstrated by Quran-internal evidence
Hlq.plain_explanation: Two occurrences concern shaving heads; one names the throat at the moment life reaches it. A geometric or encircling core could connect them, but neither Quranic context expresses that shared feature.
Hlq.strongest_counterexample: 56:83 names the throat with no cutting or hair-removal context.

Hwj.candidate_root_contribution: a felt requirement or sought purpose whose fulfillment addresses an inward or practical lack
Hwj.plain_explanation: All three haja occurrences name a purpose or need: Jacob's inward concern, practical aims carried by livestock, and needs held in breasts. The referent varies while requirement-directedness remains.
Hwj.strongest_counterexample: 12:68 can be read as a private wish rather than objective necessity, so the core must include sought purpose, not strict necessity.

Sbg.candidate_root_contribution: an imbuing treatment or quality that suffuses and characterizes what receives it
Sbg.plain_explanation: The two tokens in 2:138 present God's sibgha as a defining imbuement or characterization. The food-context sibgh in 23:20 may denote a condiment; the verse does not itself establish that suffusion/characterization is the root residue there.
Sbg.strongest_counterexample: 23:20:8:2 names sibgh for eaters and can be satisfied by condiment/relish without an explicit coloring or imbuing process.
